[[File:Eliasson_hakan.jpg|thumb|Eliasson at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2011]]
'''Lars Håkan Eliasson''' (born 13 July 1952)<ref>[http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2002015686.html Eliasson, L. H. at id.loc.gov]</ref> is a Swedish mathematician.

==Biography==
Eliasson received in 1984 his PhD from the [[Stockholm University]] under [[Jürgen Moser]] with thesis ''Hamiltonian systems with Poisson commuting integrals''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=20606}}</ref> He was a professor at the 
[[Royal Institute of Technology]] in Stockholm and then became a professor at the [[University of Paris VII]] (Denis Diderot) and the Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu of the Universities Paris VI and VII and the [[CNRS]].

His research deals with dynamical systems, quasiperiodic motion, the problem of small denominators in perturbation theory, the [[Kolmogorov–Arnold–Moser theorem#KAM Theory|KAM Theory]] and multiscale analysis in perturbation theory, Hamiltonian partial differential equations, and localization and diffusion in quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators.

In 1998 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Eliasson, L. H.|title=Reducibility and point spectrum for linear quasi-periodic skew-products|journal=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians|volume= 2|year=1998|pages=779–787|url=https://www.emis.de/journals/DMJDMV/xvol-icm/09/Eliasson.MAN.html}}</ref> In 2005 and in 2012 he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>[https://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/2311 Eliasson, Hakan | Institute for Advanced Study]</ref>

In 1990 he received the Wallenberg Prize from the [https://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Wallenberg_Prize.html Swedish Mathematical Society], 1995 he received the [[Salem Prize]], 2007 he received the Eva & Lars Gårding Prize in Mathematics and 2008 he received the [[Sophie Germain Prize]].

He was at the editorial committee of [[Acta Mathematica]] 2012–2017.
